title: A software ecosystem for multi-level provenance management in large-scale scientific workflows for AI applications
problem: Large-scale AI-based scientific workflows lack adequate multi-level provenance tracking mechanisms to capture complete data lineage and transformation history. This absence hinders experiment documentation, reproducibility verification, and performance bottleneck diagnosis.
motivation: Comprehensive provenance tracking enables reproducibility of scientific results, interpretability of AI pipeline outputs, and systematic identification of performance issues in complex workflows.
method: A coordinated set of software tools that tracks the complete lineage of data transformations throughout an AI research workflow. Starting from original data sources, the system records every processing step, creating a detailed history of how data evolves through all stages of computation. Researchers can then examine this record to document experiments, verify reproducibility, understand what happened in their pipeline, and pinpoint performance bottlenecks.
key_novelty: A coordinated ecosystem of tools designed specifically for AI research workflows that tracks data transformations at every computational level, enabling researchers to simultaneously solve documentation, reproducibility, interpretability, and performance diagnosis challenges.
contributions: Software ecosystem framework for multi-level provenance capture in scientific workflows
Provenance-enabled experiment documentation and reproducibility verification
Performance bottleneck diagnosis via provenance analysis
Provenance exploration and analysis tools for workflow understanding

metrics.other: experiment reproducibility, result interpretability, performance diagnosis capabilities

limitations: Specific implementation details, scalability evaluation, and comparative performance benchmarks not discussed.
